content: Report frame: question PRIORITY 4 asks whether NRF2 is impaired, compensatory or context-dependent in WWOX-deficient neural systems; evidence for KEAP1 reduction/NRF2 activation; separate antioxidant response from rescue and electrophile off-target from NRF2 dependence
note: Status line: closed after 5 iterations, 7 findings, 35 papers reviewed (only 19 PMIDs listed)

content: NRF2 signalling is most likely impaired/under-driven rather than compensatorily activated in WWOX-deficient neural systems (context-dependent umbrella)
note: Report states this is a prediction not a measurement

content: WWOX loss elevates GSK-3beta activation in cortex, hippocampus, cerebellum of Wwox-null mice
note: Taken from the report's "curated knowledge base"

content: Lithium (GSK-3beta inhibition) abolishes PTZ-induced seizures in Wwox-/- mice; GSK-3beta presented as validated causal seizure node
Stress-activated GSK-3beta phosphorylates Src-family kinases (Fyn/Src/Yes) driving nuclear import
Nuclear Fyn/Src phosphorylate NRF2 at Tyr568 triggering nuclear export and degradation, lowering antioxidant gene expression
Src-kinase-deficient cells show nuclear NRF2 accumulation, NRF2 target induction and reduced apoptosis
Fyn-mediated NRF2 suppression corroborated in a zinc-deficiency/diabetes model
Convergent chain WWOX loss -> up GSK-3beta -> Fyn/Src -> NRF2-Tyr568-P -> export/degradation predicts impaired NRF2 (down ARE, NQO1, HO-1, GCLC, glutathione synthesis)
Same node driving seizures predicts suppressed rather than compensatory antioxidant response; rare mechanistic convergence
GSK-3beta inhibition (e.g. lithium) attractive as NRF2-restoring strategy that also targets the validated seizure node
note: Upstream lever if baseline NRF2 is already high (L92)

content: Lithium as GSK-3beta inhibitor

Curated WWOX-DEE knowledge base holds no direct NRF2, KEAP1, glutathione, ROS or ferroptosis data; keyword audit zero hits (NRF2, KEAP1, oxidative, antioxidant, ROS, glutathione, redox, ferroptosis); "single most important limitation"

Documented WWOX-DEE mechanisms: Wnt/GSK-3beta dysregulation, impaired oligodendrocyte maturation with hypomyelination, reduced PV+/NPY+ GABAergic interneurons with lowered GAD65/67 giving E/I imbalance, cerebellar Purkinje/granule apoptosis
Wwox deletion produces neuroinflammation: activated microglia, astrogliosis, elevated Tnf-alpha/Il6
WWOX physically interacts with mitochondria and modulates ROS in a neuronal stress model
WWOX is a short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase-family oxidoreductase so a redox role is biochemically plausible but unproven in DEE
Redox involvement in WWOX-DEE is indirect and inferred only from independent literature
PV+ and NPY+ interneurons reduced and oligodendrocyte maturation impaired with Wwox loss
Gclm-KO (glutathione-synthesis-deficient) mice: selective PV-interneuron vulnerability (not calbindin/calretinin), delayed PV maturation, perineuronal-net defects, preventable by NAC
NAC preserves cortical PV interneurons and perineuronal nets and normalises EEG after oxidative injury (table: after TBI)
Perineuronal nets shield fast-spiking interneurons from oxidative stress
Schizophrenia redox review: PV interneurons and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells "more vulnerable" to oxidative stress (high metabolic load, limited antioxidant buffering)
Lost WWOX-DEE cell types are the redox-vulnerable ones, giving a bridge from antioxidant/NRF2 capacity to E/I imbalance and hypomyelination; supports case for intervention
note: Vulnerability to glutathione deficit is not NRF2 deficit per se

content: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) as NRF2-independent glutathione-repletion, antioxidant-only control arm
Sulforaphane improved white-matter integrity, oligodendrogenesis and cognition after ischemia in WT mice but "failed to provide the same level of protection in Nrf2 KO mice"
tBHQ/sulforaphane neuroprotection abolished in Nrf2-knockout cultures and rescued by adenoviral Nrf2 re-expression
Benefit lost in Nrf2-null and restored by Nrf2 re-expression defines genuine NRF2 dependence (epistasis design)
Sulforaphane protection lost in Nrf2-KO at low dose but high dose (50 mg/kg) retained partial protection via E-selectin/VCAM-1 downregulation: SFN works in part independently of Nrf2
note: Dose is a source fact only

content: Residual effect in Nrf2-null tissue = off-target thiol/electrophile chemistry, not NRF2
Decision matrix: Nrf2-KO epistasis, dose-response in Nrf2-null, genetic KEAP1 knockdown vs electrophilic drugs, NAC control arm, molecular ARE readouts separate from functional endpoints
note: Report claims designs "transfer directly" to Wwox-deficient system

content: Antioxidant-response readouts (ARE/NQO1/HO-1/GCLC, GSH) distinct from functional endpoints (seizure threshold/EEG, PV counts, myelination, survival)
RTA 408 (KEAP1 inhibitor triterpenoid) given after status epilepticus increased brain ATP, prevented neuronal death, reduced late spontaneous seizures by 94 % for at least four months
RTA 408 (triterpenoid KEAP1 inhibitor)
note: Also proposed as dose-response tool compound

content: Sulforaphane decreased ROS during epileptiform activity, restored glutathione, prevented seizure-activity-induced neuronal death in temporal-lobe epilepsy model
Sulforaphane (NRF2 activator, electrophile)
NADPH-oxidase inhibition plus NRF2 activation rendered up to 70 % of animals seizure-free eight weeks after status epilepticus
F001 evidence is from acquired insult-driven epilepsy; oxidative component is downstream of acute injury; direction of benefit cannot be assumed to transfer to genetic developmental WWOX-DEE
note: Rationale only, not WWOX proof Report L17 also asserts the models are independent and mechanistically distinct; see E76

content: Constitutive NRF2 activation in transgenic mouse hearts causes chronic reductive stress: high glutathione, reduced ROS, unresolved ER stress, misfolding/aggregation, impaired proteostasis, cardiac remodelling with diastolic dysfunction, dose-dependent, highest expressers worst

Quote: "chronic activation of Nrf2 secondary to oxidative stress is a contributing mechanism for the reductive stress-mediated heart failure"; acute activation clears ubiquitinated proteins and is protective
note: Verifier abstract reading: the quoted sentence of 24747945 is a background concern; the paper reports protection by constitutive cardiomyocyte Nrf2 activation under pressure overload, so the report table role (chronic activation can be harmful) is not the paper finding

content: NRF2 benefit is biphasic/dose- and duration-dependent; "more NRF2 is always better" unsupported; therapy must be acute, pulsatile, titratable
note: Pulsatile regimen is stated as implication, not tested Basis for chronic harm is 40729961 (cardiac); 24747945 reports protection, not harm

content: Map window between antioxidant benefit and reductive-stress harm; monitor reductive-stress markers (excess GSH, ER-stress/proteostasis readouts)
Microglial miR-155-5p binds Nrf2 3'UTR to inhibit OPC differentiation; blocking miR-155-5p promotes oligodendrocyte maturation and remyelination in cuprizone mice
Sulforaphane-driven NRF2 activation promoted oligodendrogenesis and reduced myelin loss Nrf2-dependently after ischemia
WWOX-DEE core arm is failure of OPC to oligodendrocyte maturation with falling myelination-gene transcripts; neuronal Wwox deletion gives epilepsy and myelin defects
NRF2 restoration could act as developmental/functional rescue (myelination, PV survival, E/I balance), not only antioxidant defence; NRF2 gates OPC maturation step that fails in WWOX-DEE
Cannot yet separate "NRF2 drives OPC differentiation" from "NRF2 protects OPCs from oxidative death"; needs stage-resolved experiments
Compensatorily activated NRF2 (high targets as stress response from neuroinflammation and mitochondrial ROS); less parsimonious; maladaptive if chronic
Context-dependent umbrella: NRF2 tone varies by cell type, stage, region, possibly opposite; "almost certainly true at the margins"
Impaired/under-driven hypothesis predicts low nuclear NRF2, low NQO1/HO-1/GCLC, low GSH

Model predictions: (a) low NRF2 tone in Wwox-deficient tissue; (b) normalisation by GSK-3beta/lithium; (c) NRF2-dependent functional rescue by acute KEAP1 reduction abolished in Wwox-/-;Nfe2l2-/- double mutant; (d) window bounded by reductive stress
Precondition 1 for KEAP1 reduction/NRF2 activation: demonstrate low baseline NRF2 tone (nuclear NRF2, NQO1, HO-1, GCLC, GSH/GSSG) in WWOX-deficient brain
Precondition 2: demonstrate NRF2-dependent functional benefit lost in Nrf2-null tissue and rescued by Nrf2 re-expression
If baseline NRF2 is already elevated, further activation risks reductive stress and the lever shifts upstream to GSK-3beta
Evidence convergence statement: no single paper measures NRF2 in a WWOX model; conclusion by triangulation of WWOX literature, signalling literature, redox/epilepsy literature, cardiac counterweight
No direct NRF2 measurement in any WWOX model; the three hypotheses cannot be formally adjudicated
Cross-tissue extrapolation: reductive-stress and parts of the Fyn/Src axis from cardiac, hepatic, fibroblast systems; neural windows may differ
Species/model translation: functional data mostly rodent (PTZ, cuprizone, ischemia, TBI) or in vitro; human onset in utero/infancy; postnatal window may miss prenatal lesion
GSK-3beta to NRF2 link not demonstrated in neurons of WWOX models; lithium raising NRF2 in Wwox-/- neurons untested
No biomarker for patient stratification; NRF2 tone may vary by subgroup/stage so one-size intervention could help some and harm others

Tier 1: measure nuclear vs cytoplasmic NRF2, NQO1/HO-1/GCLC transcript and protein, GSH/GSSG in Wwox-/- brain (cortex, hippocampus, cerebellum), neuronal-conditional Wwox KO and human WWOX-deletion organoids; must precede any therapeutic claim
Tier 1: single-cell/sorted PV+ interneurons and OPC/oligodendrocyte lineage, stage- and cell-type-resolved NRF2 tone
Tier 2: in Wwox-/- neurons test whether GSK-3beta inhibition raises nuclear NRF2 and ARE-target expression
Tier 3: Wwox-/- vs Wwox-/-;Nfe2l2-/- vs Wwox-/- + adenoviral/AAV Nrf2 re-expression
Tier 3: KEAP1 inhibitor/electrophile (sulforaphane, RTA 408) across doses in Nrf2-sufficient vs Nrf2-null WWOX tissue; residual high-dose effect subtracted as off-target
Tier 3: Keap1 knockdown as clean genetic NRF2 activation compared with electrophilic drugs
Tier 3: NAC run in parallel; NAC benefit not reproduced by NRF2 activation (or vice versa) dissociates glutathione repletion from NRF2 transcription programmes

Tier 4: report molecular (ARE/NQO1/HO-1/GCLC, GSH) and functional endpoints (seizure threshold/EEG, PV+ and NPY+ counts, GAD65/67, myelination transcripts, myelinated axons, axonal conductivity, survival) separately
KEAP1 (reduction/inhibition) as lever for NRF2 activation
NRF2 (Nfe2l2) restoration as the central target
GSK-3beta as upstream co-lever
Whether NRF2 is impaired, compensatory or mixed in WWOX-deficient brain by region, cell type and stage
Whether NRF2 activation gives NRF2-dependent functional rescue versus antioxidant-only or electrophile off-target benefit

Conclusion: measure baseline NRF2 first, then apply decision matrix before any therapeutic commitment; acute titratable NRF2 restoration or upstream GSK-3beta inhibition is "biologically rational candidate"
